text.p: French Open champion Gustavo Kuerten crashed out of the $535,000 Generali Open on Wednesday as quickly as Yevgeny Kafelnikov breezed into the third round.
Second-seeded Russian Kafelnikov eliminated Brazil's Fernando Meligeni 6-1 6-3 and Kuerten bowed out to unfancied Argentine Hernan Gumy, also 6-1 6-3.
After the 68-minute clay court match, fourth seed Kuerten said his poor showing was not a result of a stomach muscle injury sustained in the third round in Stuttgart last week.
"The injury is not the reason why I lost. I had a chance of reversing things at 3-2 in the second set but just didn't manage it," the Brazilian said.
World number 12 Kuerten has lost his opening matche at six tournaments this year.

When asked if his surprise French Open title had put too much pressure on him, Kuerten said: "No. Things are still the same, I win some matches and lose others. The only difference now is that more people want to see me play.
"Everyone wants to get into the top 20, the competition is tough. Once you're at the top it's difficult to stay there."
Kafelnikov, who was forced take to a four-month break earlier in the year after breaking his finger, was pleased with his performance.
"I felt good and had a lot of power today, especially at the beginning," said the Russian world number five.
